root_cause: CHG-2318 lowered the PgBouncer default_pool_size for payments-db from 60 to 25 server connections, below what payments-api needs at evening peak, so requests waited at PgBouncer and timed out after 5 s.
key_facts: PgBouncer default_pool_size was reduced from 60 to 25 by CHG-2318 on 2026-11-03.
sv_active is pinned at 25 with clients waiting, so the server pool is the bottleneck.
Same mechanism as PM-2025-007 (client demand above the PgBouncer pool).
expected_fix: Restore default_pool_size to 60 (or move the reconciliation job to a separate pool) and recheck the capacity rule.

root_cause: checkout-api v5.8.0 (CHG-2331) writes carts with plain SET and no TTL; with maxmemory-policy volatile-lru only keys that have a TTL can be evicted, so cart-cache filled to maxmemory and Redis rejected writes with OOM errors.
key_facts: CHG-2331 moved carts to CartStore, written with plain SET; the cleaner job is disabled.
volatile-lru evicts only keys with an expiry (CHG-2201, PM-2026-002); evicted_keys=0 and almost no keys have expires.
Redis returns "OOM command not allowed" when it cannot evict at maxmemory.
expected_fix: Roll back to v5.7.2 or set TTLs on cart keys; then expire or delete the TTL-less keys.

root_cause: inventory-api v3.12 (CHG-2325) added one catalog-api call of about 0.8 s per reservation message; with max.poll.records=500 a batch takes about 400 s, longer than max.poll.interval.ms of 300 s, so the consumer is evicted from the group and rebalances in a loop.
key_facts: CHG-2325 added a per-message catalog-api call of 700-900 ms.
500 records x ~0.8 s is about 400 s, above max.poll.interval.ms 300000.
Same mechanism as PM-2025-019; its action item to reduce max.poll.records (FUL-312) is still open.
expected_fix: Roll back the enrichment or lower max.poll.records (e.g. 50) and batch/cache the catalog lookups.

root_cause: Raising search-querylog-* retention from 7 to 90 days (CHG-2309) let query log indices accumulate until data nodes crossed the 95% flood-stage watermark; OpenSearch put a read-only-allow-delete block on the indices, so the indexer's writes were rejected.
key_facts: CHG-2309 increased query log retention to 90 days at about 18 GB per day.
Flood stage (95%) applies index.blocks.read_only_allow_delete.
Related disk-watermark history in PM-2025-011.
expected_fix: Delete or shrink old query log indices, revert retention, then remove the read-only block once disk is below the watermark.

root_cause: CHG-2340 cut the order-worker memory limit from 1Gi back to 512Mi based on average usage, but peak usage is about 700 MB, so pods are OOMKilled (exit 137) and crash loop.
key_facts: CHG-2340 set memory limit 512Mi (was 1Gi) from October averages.
Peak RSS is about 700 MB (PM-2026-005); the handbook says size from peak plus headroom.
expected_fix: Restore the 1Gi limit and size limits from p99 peak plus 30%.

root_cause: Paygate switched its server chain to the 'Paygate Issuing CA G3' intermediate on 2026-11-14 09:00 UTC (CHG-2302), but the payments-api trust bundle ConfigMap was never updated (PAY-881 not applied), so payments-api no longer trusts Paygate's certificate.
key_facts: CHG-2302 announced the G3 intermediate from 2026-11-14 09:00 UTC; status scheduled, not applied.
payments-api verifies Paygate against the hand-maintained ConfigMap paygate-ca-bundle.
The error is about the server chain (unknown authority), not the client certificate (renewed by cert-manager).
expected_fix: Add Paygate Issuing CA G3 to paygate-ca-bundle and restart or reload payments-api.

root_cause: CHG-2336 fixed CoreDNS at 2 replicas and disabled the proportional autoscaler; at sale-evening load the two pods saturated their CPU, and lookups across all services timed out.
key_facts: Errors in unrelated services at once point to shared infrastructure; all are DNS lookup failures.
CHG-2336 reduced CoreDNS to 2 replicas and disabled the autoscaler (min was 6).
Same mechanism as PM-2025-022; ndots:5 amplifies query volume.
expected_fix: Re-enable the proportional autoscaler (min 6) and scale CoreDNS now.

root_cause: Flyway V87 (CHG-2321) dropped idx_variant_sku and replaced it with a composite index on (product_id, sku); queries filtering on sku alone cannot use it, so the hot SKU lookup sequentially scans 42M rows.
key_facts: CHG-2321 dropped idx_variant_sku; the new composite index leads with product_id.
Lookups by sku are the hottest query; the plan shows a Seq Scan.
PM-2025-024 required EXPLAIN plans for hot queries in migration review.
expected_fix: Create an index on sku CONCURRENTLY (or restore idx_variant_sku).

root_cause: notification-service v2.4 (CHG-2328) replaced the backoff-and-Retry-After sender with the shared http-client's immediate retries; once the campaign hit the shared PostRelay limit, immediate retries burned the remaining quota and kept the account throttled.
key_facts: CHG-2328 uses up to 5 immediate retries on any non-2xx, ignoring Retry-After.
CHG-2215 had added backoff with jitter and Retry-After after PM-2026-004; v2.4 undid it.
The campaign shares the 100 messages/s PostRelay limit.
expected_fix: Configure the http-client to back off with jitter and honour Retry-After (or roll back to v2.3); pause the campaign to drain.

root_cause: inventory-api v3.13 (CHG-2333) removed the deprecated available_qty field from /v2/availability while checkout-api still requires it, so checkout-api fails to deserialize the 200 responses. The share of failures follows the inventory-api rollout.
key_facts: checkout-api has no deploy; the failing call is to inventory-api, which returns 200.
CHG-2333 removed available_qty in favour of quantity_available.
checkout-api maps the response to a strict DTO (service notes).
expected_fix: Roll back inventory-api v3.13 (or restore the field), then move checkout-api to quantity_available.

root_cause: The new daily signing-key rotation (CHG-2351) drops the old public key from the JWKS at the moment of rotation, while checkout-api keeps its JWKS for 24 hours; tokens signed with the new key carry a kid that checkout-api does not know, so it answers 401.
key_facts: CHG-2351 rotates the key daily at 06:00 UTC and publishes only the new key.
checkout-api caches the JWKS for 24 h; the log shows only yesterday's key in cache.
Same mechanism as PM-2026-009, whose action item required keeping the old key for 24 h.
checkout-api v5.9.1 (CHG-2352) does not touch token handling.
expected_fix: Publish the previous key again (keep it for at least 24 h after each rotation); flush consumer JWKS caches.

root_cause: The label-prefetch job added by CHG-2353 sends thousands of label requests every ten minutes through the same CarrierHub account, so together with normal traffic the account goes over its 50 requests/s limit and CarrierHub throttles real label and quote requests.
key_facts: CHG-2353 requests labels for about 9,000 open orders every 10 minutes on the shared account.
CarrierHub limit is 50 requests/s for quotes and labels together; logs show 71 rps and 429s.
Same mechanism as PM-2026-010, which requires a capacity check for new CarrierHub traffic.
expected_fix: Disable or throttle label-prefetch; add the client-side rate limiter (SHIP-52).

root_cause: catalog-api v8.6 (CHG-2355) moved product events to a new v2 topic and stopped writing to the old one, but the search-indexer still subscribes to the old topic, so it has received nothing since the release and new or edited products never reach the index.
key_facts: The indexer is healthy with lag 0; it simply receives no records since 2026-12-04.
CHG-2355 stopped publishing to catalog.product-updated in favour of the .v2 topic.
The synonym change (CHG-2356) is query-time only.
expected_fix: Point the search-indexer at catalog.product-updated.v2 (or republish to the old topic) and reindex products changed since the release.

root_cause: feature-flags v2.0 (CHG-2357) removed the endpoint the existing client SDKs poll; clients that start after the release get 404 and run on compiled default flags, several of which are out of date, so restarted pods show old features.
key_facts: Clients still call /api/client/features, which CHG-2357 removed; SDK 3.0 was only published that day.
Only pods that restarted are affected because running clients keep their last good values.
Same symptom pattern as PM-2026-011 (outdated compiled defaults).
expected_fix: Restore the old endpoint (or roll back feature-flags v2.0) until all clients use SDK 3.0; restart affected pods.

root_cause: The SEC-212 hardening (CHG-2359) turned off TLS session resumption and cut the keep-alive idle time to 5 s, so almost every Paygate request opens a new connection with a full mutual-TLS handshake, adding about 300 ms and a lot of CPU per authorization.
key_facts: Logs show new connections with full handshakes of about 318 ms.
CHG-2359 disabled session tickets and lowered keep-alive idle timeout to 5 s.
The logging update (CHG-2360) the same day has no functional change.
expected_fix: Restore connection reuse (longer idle timeout) and session resumption, or get a security exception for the Paygate client.

root_cause: With max.poll.records raised to 2000 (CHG-2362), one batch at about 200 ms per message takes roughly 400 s, beyond the 300 s max.poll.interval.ms, so the consumer is evicted, the batch is re-delivered and the rebalance loop keeps lag growing.
key_facts: CHG-2362 raised max.poll.records from 500 to 2000 and left max.poll.interval.ms at 300 s.
Batch time 402 s exceeds the 300 s poll interval.
Same mechanism as PM-2025-019.
expected_fix: Lower max.poll.records (to 50, as PM-2025-019 proposed) or raise max.poll.interval.ms.

root_cause: Switching off catalog-api's in-process cache (CHG-2365) sends every bundle lookup to catalog-db; inventory-api resolves bundles through catalog-api on each availability call, so checkout's stock check is slow two hops away from the change.
key_facts: The time is spent resolving bundles in inventory-api, which calls catalog-api.
CHG-2365 disabled the cache that served about 85% of catalog reads.
The gift wrap release (CHG-2366) does not touch stock calls.
expected_fix: Re-enable the catalog cache (or cache bundle lookups) while CAT-552 is investigated differently.

root_cause: Lowering the CoreDNS cache lifetime to 5 s (CHG-2368) means far fewer answers come from cache, so at sale load CoreDNS does several times more work and forwarding per lookup, saturates, and lookups time out in every service.
key_facts: Errors in unrelated services at once, all DNS lookup failures.
Cache hit ratio fell from 0.93 to 0.34 after CHG-2368 cut the cache TTL from 30 s to 5 s.
Replicas are at 6, so the older CoreDNS replica change (CHG-2336) is not the cause this time.
Same family as PM-2025-022 (CoreDNS saturation, ndots amplification).
expected_fix: Restore the 30 s cache TTL and scale CoreDNS for the sale.

root_cause: The marketing campaign uses the PostRelay account that transactional email shares, so the account sits at its 100 messages/s limit; retries already back off correctly, but confirmations simply queue behind the campaign. No change caused it; the separate sub-account from PM-2026-004 was never created.
key_facts: Retries honour Retry-After, so this is not the retry storm of PM-2026-004 or the v2.4 regression.
Account usage is at 100/100 msg/s during the campaign.
The template change (CHG-2372) did not touch sending logic.
expected_fix: Throttle or pause the campaign; create the separate transactional sub-account.

root_cause: Since v4.9 (CHG-2374) order-worker renders packing-slip PDFs itself with full-resolution product images, which pushes peak memory past the 1Gi limit on multi-item orders; the pods are OOMKilled and crash-loop.
key_facts: Crashes started after CHG-2374 moved PDF rendering in-process.
OOMKilled with a 1Gi limit while building packing slips with many images.
CHG-2361 (limit back to 1Gi) is not the cause; PM-2026-005 shows the same OOM mechanism.
expected_fix: Roll back v4.9 (or downscale images and raise the limit from measured peak plus headroom).

root_cause: The CDN rule added in CHG-2376 caches the price API at the edge for an hour, so product pages read cached prices even though catalog-api already returns the new ones.
key_facts: The CDN answers /api/price from cache (x-cache HIT, age 2410 s); catalog-api has the new price.
CHG-2376 caches /api/price/* for 1 hour.
Same mechanism as PM-2026-007; the rounding fix (CHG-2377) is unrelated.
expected_fix: Remove the /api/price/* rule and purge the CDN cache.

root_cause: Since v4.2 (CHG-2314, seven weeks earlier) remember-me sessions never expire, so session-store grew steadily until it reached its 2 GB maxmemory; with noeviction Redis rejects new session writes and sign-ins fail.
key_facts: Most keys have no expiry (keys 2.28M, expires 0.39M).
CHG-2314 stores remember-me sessions without a TTL; about 40 MB of sessions per day accumulate.
session-store uses noeviction, so a full store rejects writes.
expected_fix: Give remember-me sessions a TTL (e.g. 30 days), clean up old keys, raise memory temporarily.

root_cause: Scaling payments-api to 10 replicas (CHG-2380) without resizing PgBouncer raised peak client demand to around 200 connections against 60 server connections, so at the evening peak requests queue at PgBouncer and time out.
key_facts: sv_active pinned at 60 with 84 clients waiting.
CHG-2380 raised replicas to 10 with 20 connections each; the pool stayed at 60 (CHG-2354).
Same mechanism as PM-2025-007 (scaled the app but not the pooler).
expected_fix: Apply the PM-2025-007 capacity rule (raise default_pool_size with headroom or lower per-replica pools).

root_cause: CHG-2383 switched cart-cache to allkeys-lru, so when memory is full Redis evicts any key, including carts that customers are still using, instead of only keys with a TTL.
key_facts: evicted_keys is high with policy allkeys-lru.
CHG-2383 changed the policy back to allkeys-lru, undoing CHG-2201.
Same mechanism as PM-2026-002.
expected_fix: Restore volatile-lru and fix the memory pressure (TTLs, cleaner, more memory).

root_cause: Migration V93 (CHG-2386) rewrites every product_variant row in one long transaction, holding row locks for its whole duration; reads that need those rows wait, hit the lock timeout, and storefront calls to catalog-api time out.
key_facts: A Flyway session has held locks on product_variant for 24 minutes.
CHG-2386 backfills all 42M rows in a single transaction at deploy.
The storefront deploy (CHG-2387) does not touch product pages.
expected_fix: Cancel the migration transaction; redo the backfill in small batches.

root_cause: shipping-api v2.4 (CHG-2389) renamed the label response field that order-worker copies into the warehouse hand-off, so order-worker fails on the missing field even though labels are created successfully.
key_facts: Response keys now contain tracking_id instead of tracking_number.
order-worker requires tracking_number for the hand-off (service notes).
The concurrency change (CHG-2390) does not change the hand-off.
expected_fix: Roll back shipping-api v2.4 or return both fields, then update order-worker.

root_cause: Applying fuzzy matching to every text field (CHG-2392) multiplies the work per query on large fields like description and attributes; search-prod, sized for title-only fuzziness, runs out of CPU and latency rises.
key_facts: The slow log shows fuzziness AUTO across description, brand and attributes.
CHG-2392 extended fuzziness from title to all fields.
Cluster was sized for about 35% CPU with title-only fuzziness.
expected_fix: Revert fuzziness to the title field (or restrict to short fields) and re-measure.

root_cause: CHG-2395 made every flag client poll once a second instead of every 30 s, a roughly 30-fold load increase on a flag service sized for the old interval; it saturates, fetches time out and pods wait for flags at startup.
key_facts: feature-flags handles about 412 req/s (sized for about 13 at a 30 s interval) at 98% CPU.
CHG-2395 lowered the polling interval for all clients via the server setting.
Clients fall back to defaults when fetches fail (PM-2026-011).
expected_fix: Restore the 30 s interval (use push or a separate kill-switch channel instead).

root_cause: CHG-2399 had cert-manager re-issue the Paygate client certificate from the new internal CA, which Paygate does not trust; Paygate rejects the mutual-TLS handshake from the moment the new certificate was loaded.
key_facts: The error comes from Paygate's side (remote error, unknown certificate authority).
The client certificate is now issued by Kestrel Internal CA v2 since 2027-01-10 22:00 (CHG-2399).
Paygate only accepts certificates from Kestrel Partner CA; the server-chain issue (CHG-2302) is unrelated.
expected_fix: Re-issue paygate-client from the Kestrel Partner CA issuer and exclude it from the CA consolidation.

root_cause: Raising the inventory-api HPA ceiling to 24 (CHG-2401) lets the sale scale it to 21 pods with 10 connections each, past inventory-db's limit of 150 connections, so new connections are refused and availability calls fail.
key_facts: 21 replicas x 10 connections = 210 > max_connections 150.
CHG-2401 raised the HPA maximum from 8 to 24 without changing the pool.
expected_fix: Cap replicas so the pools fit, or add a pooler in front of inventory-db.

root_cause: CHG-2403 made the session cookie SameSite=Strict, and browsers do not send Strict cookies on the cross-site redirect back from the bank's 3-D Secure page, so the storefront sees no session at /checkout/return.
key_facts: The return request comes from the bank's site and arrives without the session cookie.
CHG-2403 changed SameSite from Lax to Strict; Lax was chosen for this redirect.
expected_fix: Revert the session cookie to SameSite=Lax.

root_cause: With the carrier rate cache switched off (CHG-2406), every checkout quote goes live to CarrierHub; quotes now take close to 3 s and push the shared account into rate limiting, so checkout's 3 s quote call times out.
key_facts: Logs show cache=disabled and CarrierHub calls of about 2.7 s plus 429s.
CHG-2406 disabled the 15-minute rate cache (about 92% hit rate).
Quotes and labels share the 50 requests/s limit (PM-2026-010).
expected_fix: Re-enable the rate cache (shorter TTL if freshness matters).

root_cause: CHG-2410 moved the sender to the new mail.kestrel.example domain before its SPF and DKIM records existed, so PostRelay permanently rejects the unauthenticated messages.
key_facts: 550 5.7.26 for the new sender domain.
CHG-2410 changed the From domain while DNS records were only requested (NET-118).
The template engine release (CHG-2409) was rolled back.
expected_fix: Switch the sender back to orders@kestrel.example until SPF/DKIM are published; resend failed emails.

root_cause: catalog-api v8.9 (CHG-2413) loads attributes with a separate query for each variant, and that query has no index on variant_id, so each product request runs many sequential scans.
key_facts: Tens of millions of per-variant attribute queries, each a Seq Scan.
CHG-2413 added one query per variant to the product response.
The index (CHG-2414) is dated after the incident; PM-2025-024 required EXPLAIN plans for hot queries.
expected_fix: Roll back v8.9 or batch the attribute query, and add the variant_id index.

root_cause: Raising the Paygate request timeout to 15 s (CHG-2417) means that during Paygate's slowdown each payment holds a checkout worker thread for up to 15 s instead of failing fast at 2 s; checkout's 50 payment threads fill up and new payments are rejected.
key_facts: payments-api waits almost 14 s for Paygate; checkout's 50-thread payment pool is exhausted.
CHG-2417 raised the timeout from 2 s to 15 s the day before.
expected_fix: Restore the 2 s timeout (or add a circuit breaker on Paygate calls).

root_cause: Autovacuum on the reservations table was switched off for the stock import (CHG-2364) six weeks ago and never turned back on; with millions of updates a day, dead rows piled up and the bloated table makes every reservation and availability query slower.
key_facts: 412M dead tuples and 61 GB; last autovacuum on 2026-12-11.
CHG-2364 disabled autovacuum on reservations, to be re-enabled after the import (FUL-401).
Slow per-message processing leads to lag as in PM-2025-019.
expected_fix: Re-enable autovacuum, run VACUUM (or pg_repack) on reservations.
